title: Income-tax Authorities
outcomes: Identify income-tax authorities and limits on CBDT instructions.
Apply jurisdiction, transfer and faceless provisions.
Apply search, seizure and requisition powers and timelines.

meta.exam_tip: Contrast search and survey: seizure, oath, timing and retention limits.

concepts.title: Classes of authorities, instructions and charter
body: Section 236 lists income-tax authorities: the CBDT (constituted under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963), Principal Directors-General/Principal Chief Commissioners, Directors-General/Chief Commissioners, Principal Directors/Principal Commissioners, Directors/Commissioners including CIT(Appeals), Additional and Joint Directors/Commissioners, Deputy and Assistant Directors/Commissioners, Income-tax Officers, Tax Recovery Officers and Inspectors.

Section 239 lets the CBDT issue orders, instructions and directions to subordinate authorities, which they must follow — but it cannot require any authority to make a particular assessment or dispose of a case in a particular manner, nor interfere with CIT(Appeals). Circulars relaxing provisions for taxpayers are binding on the department.

Section 240 empowers the CBDT to adopt and publish a Taxpayer's Charter setting out the department's commitments (fairness, courtesy, timely decisions) and taxpayers' expectations (honesty, compliance, record-keeping).
concepts.analogy: The CBDT guides but cannot dictate an assessment.
concepts.work: A CBDT circular extending a filing date binds every AO.

concepts.title: Jurisdiction and faceless proceedings
body: Section 241 lets the CBDT and higher authorities direct which authorities exercise jurisdiction by area, persons, income or cases; higher authorities can exercise lower authorities' powers. Section 242 confers jurisdiction on AOs; an assessee can question jurisdiction only within prescribed time.

Section 243 permits transfer of cases between AOs after giving an opportunity of being heard (except where transfer is within the same city or locality). Section 244 lets a successor authority continue proceedings from where they stood.
Section 245 enables faceless jurisdiction: the CBDT may notify schemes under which functions are performed electronically with dynamic allocation of cases and no physical interface.
concepts.analogy: Jurisdiction flows from directions; faceless schemes remove the face-to-face meeting.
concepts.work: A case transferred from Pune to Mumbai requires a hearing before the order.

concepts.title: Search, seizure and requisition
body: Section 246 gives authorities civil-court powers (discovery, summons, production of documents, commissions). Section 247: on information that a person has failed to produce documents, would not produce them, or holds undisclosed money, bullion, jewellery, virtual digital assets or valuables, specified authorities may authorise a search. The authorised officer can enter, break open locks, search persons, seize books and assets (stock-in-trade is only inventoried), and record statements on oath that can be used as evidence. Reasons to believe are not disclosed to the assessee (section 249).
Section 248: requisition of books or assets held by other authorities. Section 251 presumes seized books and assets belong to the person searched and that their contents are true.

Section 250: seized assets may be applied against existing liabilities. The person may apply for release within 30 days from the end of the month of seizure; if source is explained, liabilities recovered and approval obtained, assets are released within 120 days of the last authorisation. The Government pays 0.5% interest per month on excess seized money from 120 days after the last authorisation until assessment.
concepts.analogy: Search is the most intrusive power; strict timelines protect the taxpayer.
concepts.work: Excess seized money of ₹15 lakh for 10 months earns interest of ₹75,000.

concepts.title: Survey and power to call for information
body: Section 253 (survey): an authority may enter business, professional or charitable premises within jurisdiction during working hours (business premises) or between sunrise and sunset (other places) to inspect books, verify cash, stock and valuables, place marks of identification, make inventories and record statements on oath that may be relevant to any proceeding under the Act (section 253(5)).

The officer may impound books but not remove cash or stock, recording reasons and retaining them for up to 15 days (excluding holidays) unless approval for longer retention is obtained. A survey can also be conducted after a function or ceremony to check expenditure.

Sections 252, 254 and 255 empower authorities to call for information from any person, collect information for verification and inspect company registers; section 260 enables faceless collection of information.
concepts.analogy: Survey verifies on the spot; search takes away.
concepts.work: Books impounded in a survey cannot be kept beyond 15 working days without approval.

illustrations.title: Interest on excess seized money
illustrations.q: In a search, ₹50,00,000 cash was seized from Navin. ₹5,00,000 was released under section 250(2). No assets were sold. Liabilities determined on assessment were ₹30,00,000. The interest period (from the day after 120 days of the last authorisation to completion of assessment) is 10 months. Compute interest payable by the Government.

illustrations.q: The last authorisation for a search on Seema was executed on 15 June 2026, when jewellery was seized. By when must she apply for release, and by when must the AO release the assets if the conditions are met?

summary: Section 247 search; 250 seized assets: 30 days, 120 days, 0.5% interest.
Section 253 survey: impound up to 15 days.
remember: Survey cannot seize cash or stock.
traps: Assuming cash or stock can be seized in a survey.

viva.q: What is the purpose of the Taxpayer's Charter?
viva.model: To set out the department's commitments to taxpayers and what it expects from taxpayers.

viva.q: Can statements be recorded on oath during a survey under the 2025 Act?
viva.model: Yes, section 253(5) allows the authority to record statements on oath useful for any proceeding under the Act.

viva.q: What presumption arises about seized books?
viva.model: They are presumed to belong to the person searched and their contents are presumed true.
Electronic performance of functions with dynamic allocation of cases and no physical interface.

viva.q: Within what time must seized assets be released?
viva.model: Within 120 days from the last authorisation, if conditions are met.
